name: Grundregeln für Gäste, die eine Unterkunft gebucht haben
text: Airbnb Help Center article 2894 (German; page date unknown, 2026-01-01 default) is the guest ground rules page, not the new host house rules policy. It states guests should leave the place without need for intensive or deep cleaning, that host cleaning fees only cover standard cleaning between stays, and that hosts may not charge fees for not completing certain cleaning tasks at checkout. It does not mention the 20 Nov 2026 policy or its effective date.

name: Airbnb Q3 2026 financial results
text: Airbnb newsroom, 5 Nov 2026 (primary): Q3 revenue +19% YoY to $4.9 billion, GBV +21% to $27.7 billion, nights and seats booked +16%, net income $1.9 billion, adjusted EBITDA +22% to $2.5 billion (52% margin). New authorization to repurchase up to an additional $12 billion of Class A stock. Q4 2026 revenue guided to $3.22 to $3.28 billion (+16% to 18%); FY2026 revenue growth now high teens, adjusted EBITDA margin about 36%. AI assistant resolved about 40% of support issues without a human (a third in Q2); own AI agent rollout planned for first half 2027. Redesigned multi-listing calendar: nearly 1 in 4 eligible hosts opted in during early access. Amex partnership launched 22 Oct; thousands of hotels in 60+ destinations.

name: Best AI Guest Messaging for Short-Term Rentals (2026)
text: Ranking of eight AI messaging tools by Conduit, itself a ranked vendor (last updated 7 Oct 2026; low confidence on competitors). Hospitable is the only one of the five PMS vendors listed: AI Suggested Replies, Q&A Auto Replies, Message AI Assistant, Inbox AI (fully automated messaging on the Mogul plan), AI Issue Alerts, AI Copilot; free Essentials plan exists. Guesty and Hostaway appear only as PMSs that third-party AI tools (Conduit, Aeve, Enso, HostBuddy) connect to, not with native AI. Lodgify and Smoobu are not covered natively.

name: Consumo exige a dos plataformas la retirada de 8.300 anuncios de alojamientos turísticos que se ofertan como alquileres de temporada
text: Ministry press release (primary), 22 Oct 2026. Consumo asked two platforms to remove 8,318 listings advertised as seasonal rentals while allowing bookings under 31 days, the minimum under Real Decreto-ley 29/2026 (approved 6 Oct 2026). 6,772 are in Comunidad de Madrid, 6,523 in Madrid city. Viewed as misleading practice under art. 47 TRLGDCU. Notices sent via DSA notification mechanisms; platforms become directly liable and non-removal could open a sanctioning file. Cites earlier EUR 64 million sanction on Airbnb (65,000+ listings removed) and Booking removing 4,000+ listings.

name: Consumo requiere a dos grandes plataformas de alquiler turístico que retiren más de 8.000 anuncios ilícitos tras el bloqueo de casi 4.500 sólo en Madrid
text: Ministry press release (primary), Madrid 12 Nov 2026. Consumo told two large tourist-rental platforms (not named) to remove 8,352 listings advertised without a valid registration. Breakdown: 7,199 on platform one, 1,153 on platform two; no registration number 7,227 (6,263 + 964); false number 1,125 (936 + 189), being extinct room-rental numbers used for whole units. Follows the 22 Oct action in which 4,443 Madrid listings were blocked in Spain (extinct seasonal registration under Real Decreto 1312/2024, bookings of 1 to 30 nights). Those stay visible from non-Spanish IPs; Andrés Barragán wrote to the Ayuntamiento de Madrid asking it to request blocking abroad under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. No deadline or fine amount stated.

name: Consumo ordena retirar 8.352 anuncios turísticos ilegales
text: Rewrite of the ministry release, 12 Nov 2026. Ministry ordered two unnamed platforms to remove 8,352 listings: 7,199 on first, 1,153 on second; 7,227 without registration number, 1,125 with non-authentic (expired room-rental) numbers. Adds to 22 Oct action blocking 4,443 Madrid listings. Andrés Barragán sent a letter to the Ayuntamiento de Madrid with ID, URL, UTC verification date and minimum booking (1 to 30 nights) of each listing so it can get them blocked abroad.

name: Airbnb removes listings following pressure from Consumer Affairs
text: Europa Press-based report, 30 Oct 2026, on the 22 Oct action (more than 8,300 listings on two platforms, including Airbnb). Airbnb says it already took the requested measures and notified hosts, but criticised the lack of a defined framework and competence conflicts between administrations causing unnecessary confusion, calling for fair and proportionate regulation. Ministry sees misleading practice under art. 47 TRLGDCU; platforms assume direct responsibility, non-removal could lead to a sanctioning procedure. Recalls EUR 64M Airbnb sanction (65,000+ listings) and Booking removing 4,000+.

name: Verschärftes Regulativ für Kurzzeitvermietung in Wien
text: DFZ (Hannes Neumayer), 20.10.2026: Die Koalition aus SPÖ und NEOS brachte am Dienstag einen Initiativeintrag ein, der im Wohnbau-Ausschuss mit Stimmen von SPÖ, NEOS, FPÖ und Grünen eine Mehrheit fand; endgültig soll der Landtag beschließen (kein Datum genannt). Bauordnung: neuer § 7g, mindestens 80 Prozent Wohnnutzfläche, mindestens drei Zimmereinheiten, gesonderter Straßenzugang; Verfahren ab 11. Oktober nach neuem Recht. Privatausnahme 90 Tage nur für eine Wohnung mit aufrechtem Wohnsitz. Register pro Wohneinheit, Plattformen müssen stichprobenartig kontrollieren und unzulässige Inserate entfernen. Strafen bis 50.000 Euro, Register ab 1. Jänner 2027, Übergang bis Ende März 2027. Zitate: Ludwig, Hanel-Torsch, Arapović, Baupolizei-Leiter Ilja Messner.

name: Commission to investigate how Booking.com combats scams and fraud under the Digital Services Act
text: European Commission news item (dated 2026-10-21, updated 22 October 2026): the Commission opened formal proceedings to assess whether Booking.com may have breached the Digital Services Act by not diligently assessing or mitigating risks from fraudulent listings and phishing scams, and on transparency for not clearly labelling as ads listings whose providers paid for higher ranking. Three focus areas: fraudulent and non-compliant listings; phishing scams exploiting reservation and guest data; paid-for boosted listings not identifiable as ads. Primary source.

name: Airbnb guests no longer have to wash dishes or strip beds. Furious hosts are threatening to boycott and raise cleaning fees
text: Fortune (Lena Borrelli), 28 Oct 2026: Under a “reasonable house rules and requests” policy announced 20 Oct, Airbnb hosts can no longer ask guests to do tasks needing significant effort (strip bed, take trash offsite, wash dishes). It applies worldwide to reservations booked on or after 20 Nov 2026; existing bookings unaffected. Seven standard rules (max guests, quiet hours, events, pets, smoking, commercial photography, lock-up); no host fines (AirCover instead), no new rules after booking. Sanctions: warnings, listing notice, reduced search visibility. A Change.org petition has topped 10,000 signatures, up from more than 5,000 reported by CBS News days earlier; some hosts plan a booking blackout on 20 Nov and some threaten higher prices or leaving. Airbnb does not cap cleaning fees.

name: Vrbo's 12% Commission: New Host Fees From Oct 29, 2026
text: Futurestay (author Phil Kennard): Vrbo announced on 29 Sep 2026 a flat 12% commission from 29 Oct 2026 for hosts and property managers, including PMS-connected ones. Previously most pay-per-booking hosts paid about 8% (5% plus 3% processing) and PMS-connected hosts 5%. Charged on rent plus guest fees, not taxes. Futurestay says Vrbo's help page calls it all-in but still listed a 3% processing fee, so Vrbo's share could be about $150 per $1,000 instead of $120 (this conflicts with the current help page). To keep payout, pay-per-booking hosts need about +4.5% and PMS hosts about +8%. New host terms require Vrbo rates, discounts and fees to be at least as favorable as the host's own website, and let Vrbo charge commission on direct bookings from a Vrbo inquiry within 30 days. Subscription listings switch at term end; Skift reports guest fees of 11-14% may be reduced.

name: Guesty acquires Smily, deepening its investment in France's booming short-term rental market
text: Guesty press release, 17 Sep 2026 (New York & Paris): Guesty has completed the acquisition of Smily (formerly BookingSync), a leading PMS and channel manager in France founded 2005 by Sébastien Grosjean, open to paying customers since 2010. Terms not disclosed; all five Smily founders and some shareholders reinvest part of the proceeds in Guesty equity. Smily processed more than €3.3bn in bookings for 13 million travelers and is a Booking.com Premier Plus Connectivity Partner for 2026. Guesty says it runs 500,000+ properties in 100+ countries, has $410m funding (KKR, Apax Digital, etc.) and shipped 300+ features in 2026.

name: Vrbo Service Fee: Commission Structure Change
text: Hospitable support article (updated Nov 2026): Vrbo's 12% commission began rolling out 29 Oct 2026, staggered per account. It applies to Pay-Per-Booking hosts now and Pay-Per-Subscription hosts when their annual term ends, whether or not they use a PMS; it includes Vrbo's payment processing and Vrbo does not discount it for third-party processors. Hospitable as merchant of record adds 3.9% (2.7% AU). Commission is on nightly rate plus host fees (cleaning, pet, boat); taxes and refundable deposits are separate. Vrbo bills fees to the card on file. Hospitable automatically raised Vrbo markups on 29 Oct (opt-out closed 28 Oct 23:59 PT) so payout stays flat, e.g. 10% markup at 8% commission becomes 15% at 12%; Vrbo Partner connection hosts can include fees. Vrbo Legacy listings are re-priced by Vrbo (first 12 months of dates first).

name: Vrbo's New 12% Commission: What It Means & How to Prepare
text: Hostaway says Vrbo moves pay-per-booking hosts to a standard 12% commission from Thursday 29 Oct 2026, applied to bookings made from that date (not stay date). Previously PMS-connected hosts paid 5%; hosts without PMS paid 5% plus 3% processing; annual subscribers move at subscription expiry as Vrbo retires the Pay-Per-Subscription program. The 12% covers rental amount plus guest fees such as cleaning and pet fees, and includes payment processing; Australia, Europe and New Zealand may be higher. To keep a 5% net payout prices must rise about 7.95% (950/0.88), not 7%. Hostaway offers a Vrbo-specific whole-number markup (Listings > Price & Fees) and a Vrbo Host Channel Fee setting of 12% for reporting; it recommends changes by 28 Oct.

name: Airbnb Floats Price-Matching: How AI Agents and Direct Bookings Are Reshaping Travel Value
text: The Hype Magazine (Dr Jerry Doby), 21 Nov 2026. Affiliate-linked rewrite of the Skift article ('Originally referenced from skift.com'), same headline stem. Repeats Chesky's quote and Skift's 16-listing Instinct test (direct cheaper in 10, 1% to 42%). Adds details not visible in Skift's truncated text and unverified here: Uniko Living in Mexico City $145 on Airbnb vs $84 direct; hotels mostly won direct while apartments split 3-3 with one tie; a '45 listings scanned, 23 without direct portal' figure that conflicts with the 16-listing framing; Savvy CEO Eric Goldreyer on price-match options; Vrbo parity clauses. Not independent.

name: El Gobierno pide la retirada de más de 8.300 anuncios ilícitos de pisos turísticos
text: EFE wire via Infobae, 12 Nov 2026. Consumo (minister Pablo Bustinduy) demanded removal of 8,352 listings advertised without licence or with a false registration number on two large platforms: 7,227 lack identification, 1,125 use an extinct number of room rentals though offering whole homes. Follows 22 Oct action on 4,443 Madrid listings blocked in Spain; ministry warned the Ayuntamiento de Madrid the platform keeps them visible from non-Spanish IPs and urged it to request blocking abroad. Platforms unnamed.

name: Wien dreht Airbnb den Hahn zu – das ändert sich ab 2027
text: KOSMO, 22.10.2026: behauptet, der Wiener Landtag habe am 20. Oktober 2026 die strengeren Regeln beschlossen (Bauordnung plus Kurzzeitvermietungsregister), mit Stimmen von SPÖ, NEOS, FPÖ und Grünen; ÖVP kritisiert fehlendes Begutachtungsverfahren. Das widerspricht DFZ, wonach am 20.10. nur der Wohnbau-Ausschuss entschied. Register startet 1. Jänner 2027, Übergang für bereits inserierte Wohnungen bis Ende März 2027, Plattformen müssen kontrollieren und Inserate entfernen, bis 50.000 Euro Strafe als Höchstbetrag, 90-Tage-Ausnahme nur eine Wohnung.

name: Top 5 Guesty Competitors & Alternatives to Try in 2026
text: Lodgify's own comparison page (last updated October 2026; competitor claims low confidence). Lodgify has a unified inbox with built-in AI writing assistant to draft guest replies, and Lodgify AI Co-Host in early access (prepares actions for approval). Guesty's small-host product Guesty for Hosts was sunset in 2026 and folded into Guesty Lite (1-3 listings). Hostaway markets AI-generated guest replies; Hospitable: AI Guest Issue Alerts from Host plan, Mogul adds fully automated messaging via InboxAI. Smoobu: paid-only from 2026, plans Professional Flex ~EUR 29, Pre-Paid ~EUR 35, Teams Pro+ ~EUR 55; no AI mentioned.

name: El ultimátum del Ministerio de Consumo a los alquileres turísticos: 8.300 anuncios ilegales que deben desaparecer
text: Explainer, 16 Nov 2026 (Diego Servente), based on the ministry release. 8,352 listings on two unnamed platforms (7,199 and 1,153); per-platform split 6,263/964 no number, 936/189 false. 4,443 Madrid listings blocked in Spain but visible abroad; letter by Andrés Barragán cites Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. Mentions RD 1312/2024 extinct seasonal registry and RDL 29/2026 (6 Oct, stays 31 days to 12 months). Adds, without attribution to the release, that illicit advertising may be a grave infraction with fines up to EUR 100,000, exceedable by four to six times the illicit benefit. No deadline stated.

name: Airbnb Expands Hotel Push With Price Match, Bigger Rebates
text: NerdWallet (Benjamin Din), 20 May 2026, from Airbnb's 2026 Summer Release event in San Francisco. Airbnb adds independent and boutique (non-chain) hotels in select cities such as London, New York, Madrid, Paris, Rome and Singapore. Listings with a 'featured hotel' badge give up to 15% back in Airbnb credit (up from up to 10%), credited within 24 hours of checkout and usable within one year. Select hotel listings carry a price-match guarantee: if the same stay is cheaper elsewhere, the difference is paid as Airbnb credit, up to $400, usable within a year. Conditions: booking must show eligibility at checkout; the lower rate needs the same dates, room type, guest count and a cancellation policy no stricter than Airbnb's.

name: Wien verschärft Regeln für Airbnb
text: ORF Wien, 19.09.2026: Bürgermeister Ludwig (SPÖ) kündigte im Sommergespräch strengere Regeln an. Das WKVRG soll noch im November im Landtag beschlossen werden, Inkrafttreten 1. Jänner 2027, Übergangsfrist für bestehende Angebote bis Ende des ersten Quartals 2027, Strafen bis 50.000 Euro. Umwidmungen werden eingeschränkt (80 Prozent Wohnnutzung). Reaktionen: Mietervereinigung (Georg Niedermühlbichler) begrüßt, Verband der Apartmentvermieter (VDAV) grundsätzlich positiv aber Kritik an Umsetzung, FPÖ (Dominik Nepp) spricht von Nebelkerze, Grüne (Judith Pühringer) fordern mehr.

name: Kurzzeitvermietung: Beschluss am Dienstag
text: ORF Wien, 16.10.2026: Bürgermeister Ludwig kündigt an, dass der Landtag am Dienstag (20.10.) weitere Verschärfungen bei Kurzzeitvermietung beschließen soll: Register mit Pflichtnummer ab Jahresbeginn 2027, drei Monate Übergangsfrist, Plattformen wie Airbnb und Booking.com müssen Angaben prüfen und ungültige Inserate entfernen. Umwidmung erschwert (80 Prozent Wohnnutzung), rückwirkend für Ansuchen seit 10. Oktober. Bestehende 90-Tage-Regel seit 2024 bleibt.

name: Landtag beschloss neue AirBnB-Regeln
text: ORF Wien, 20.10.2026: Der Wiener Landtag hat die neuen Regeln für Kurzzeitvermietung beschlossen. Ab 1. Jänner 2027 müssen sich alle Kurzzeitvermieter registrieren; ohne Nummer kein Inserat; Plattformen dürfen nur registrierte Angebote zulassen. Drei Monate Übergangsfrist, ab April droht ohne Registrierung das Aus. Parallel verschärfte Umwidmungsregeln: mindestens 80 Prozent eines Gebäudes bleiben Wohnzwecken vorbehalten. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig (SPÖ) spricht von Schlupflöchern; der Verband der Apartmentvermieter widerspricht.

name: Bürgermeister Ludwig: Wien ist Vorbild beim Schutz von leistbaren Wohnungen für die Bevölkerung
text: OTS-Presseaussendung des Büros Bürgermeister Ludwig vom 19.09.2026, inhaltsgleich mit der Stadt-Wien-Seite: WKVRG soll noch im November im Wiener Landtag beschlossen werden, Inkrafttreten 1. Jänner 2027, Übergangsfrist für bereits angebotene Wohnungen bis Ablauf des 1. Quartals 2027. Registrierungsnummer in Inseraten Pflicht, Strafen bis 50.000 Euro pro Verstoß, Mindeststrafen 2.000 Euro bei Wiederholung, Umwidmung nur bei mindestens 80 Prozent Wohnnutzfläche. Kontakt: Mario Dujakovic, Mediensprecher.

name: Airbnb targets first-half 2027 for AI agent launch
text: PhocusWire (Cathy Walsh), 6 Nov 2026: On the Q3 call (Thu 5 Nov) CEO Brian Chesky said Airbnb will begin rolling out its AI travel agent in the first half of 2027, with a generative UI of hundreds of travel components; sponsored listings follow the agent launch. Q3 revenue rose 19% to $4.9 billion (16% ex-FX), ADR up 4%, GBV up 21% to $27.7 billion, nights and seats booked up 16% to 155 million (reserve now, pay later added about 3 points). Net income $1.9 billion, adjusted EBITDA up 22% to $2.5 billion. App nights up 29% (66% of nights). Amex partnership: thousands of bookings, nearly a quarter from new travelers. Airbnb handles nearly half a million bookings a day.

name: European Commission investigating Booking.com's handling of scams, fraud
text: PhocusWire (Abby Crotty): the Commission launched a DSA investigation into Booking.com after a preliminary probe covering risk assessment reports from 2023 to 2026 and information requests in September 2025 and May 2026. Booking.com has been a VLOP since April 2023; fines up to 6% of global annual turnover are possible. The opening of formal proceedings allows interim measures and a non-compliance finding; Booking.com can settle with commitments. Booking.com says it is cooperating fully. Commission EVP Henna Virkkunen is quoted. Booking.com confirmed a data breach in April 2026 and was designated a DMA gatekeeper in May 2024.

name: Guesty For Hosts has shut down: how to choose a replacement (and the part most guides miss)
text: Recal (an ops-tool vendor, low confidence on competitors). Guesty For Hosts shut down on 31 May 2026; technical support ended 15 January. Automated messages, templates and pricing rules did not transfer, not even to Guesty Lite and Pro. Recommends Smoobu (basic scheduled messaging), Hospitable (strongest, full automation plus AI reply drafts), Lodgify (AI reply drafts, no full automation), Hostaway (full, advanced messaging, quote-based pricing).

name: Airbnb Floats Price-Matching: A Skift Test Shows Where Direct Booking Wins
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 20 Nov 2026. Using the AI agent Instinct, Skift compared 16 Airbnb listings with the properties' own website rates: direct was cheaper in 10, by as much as 42%, and one was essentially a tie. When an X account asked whether Airbnb profits would suffer if AI agents compared prices before booking, CEO Brian Chesky replied 'You presume we could never offer a price-match guarantee.' Skift stresses this was not an announcement for short-term rentals (Airbnb recently started price-matching for hotels) but a signal Airbnb could, and may eventually have to. Fetched text is truncated at about 1,000 characters (paywall); the rest of the article was not available.

name: Airbnb’s New Policy for Hosts: Don’t Ask Guests to Wash Dishes or Strip Beds
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 21 Oct 2026: In a Tuesday (20 Oct) email titled “Important Changes to House Rules”, Airbnb told hosts that starting November 20 they can choose from seven standard house rules and are “generally not allowed” to ask guests to wash dishes, strip beds or take out the garbage. It is the first published Airbnb house rules policy spelling out reasonable host requests. Repeat violators could get a notice on the listing, lower search visibility or other actions under the terms of service (cancelled bookings, loss of Superhost or Guest Favorite status, account suspension). A new terms provision bars hosts from requiring separate rental agreements, with exceptions (monthly stays, Airbnb Luxe, optional amenities). Article text is truncated at the source.

name: Airbnb Pitches Hotels: We Care More About Stays Than Booking.com Does
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 18 Nov 2026. Airbnb is courting independent hotels with a pitch aimed at Booking.com: unlike Booking, it says, it is built around stays. Lou Zameryka, Airbnb's global head of hotel enterprise and connectivity partnerships, told Skift on Wednesday (18 Nov) after speaking at the Phocuswright conference in Hollywood, Florida, that Booking is 'not hotel-centric'. Fetched text is truncated at about 490 characters (paywall); no commission figures or further executives are available.

name: Airbnb Updates House Rules After Host Pushback
text: Skift (Dennis Schaal), 16 Nov 2026 (listed as “Airbnb Makes Concessions on House Rules After Host Pushback”): Airbnb partially walked back the October policy after public host objections, but the core restrictions still take effect 20 Nov 2026. Under the 3 Nov update “Requests” become “additional rules” that guests “are expected to comply with”, covering dishes in the sink, used towels, recycling. Hosts may require a separate rental agreement when an insurer demands one. Still barred: checkout chores, host-imposed fines, rules added after booking, collecting guest IDs, emails, phone numbers or signed agreements absent a legal, building or insurer requirement. Review timeline: listing reviews run 20 Nov 2026 to March 2027, at least 20 days to fix, one appeal per flagged rule. Hosts can cancel without penalty only if a guest breaks one of the seven standard rules.

name: Top AI Tools for Vacation Rental Automation in 2026: The Ultimate Guide
text: Smoobu's own blog (vendor self-description). Smoobu's AI translates message templates into 10 languages; every translation is marked 'Translated with AI' for review. AI translation of guest messages and replies in the inbox is rolling out one account at a time. Smoobu has no ChatGPT or Gemini built in; hosts should draft with external AI and paste in. Lists third-party tools (Breezeway Assist, HostBuddy AI, Conduit, PriceLabs, Enso Connect) for AI messaging. Page date 2026-02-11 per metadata; text does not date the rollout. No AI reply drafting or auto-reply is claimed for Smoobu.

name: Spain orders removal of 8,352 illegal tourist rental adverts
text: English-language rewrite, 18 Nov 2026. Ministry of Consumer Affairs ordered two unidentified platforms to remove 8,352 listings: 7,199 on one, 1,153 on another; 7,227 no registration number, 1,125 invalid. Madrid listings (4,443, October) blocked in Spain remain visible abroad; ministry asked Madrid City Council to pursue removal under EU digital services law. Context: Barcelona Airbnb listings down 20% in a year, city plans to eliminate about 10,000 licensed tourist apartments by Nov 2028.

name: Bürgermeister Ludwig: Registrierungspflicht für Kurzzeitvermietungen ab 1. Jänner 2027
text: Stadt Wien (Primärquelle): Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig kündigt ein neues Wiener Kurzzeitvermietungsregistergesetz (WKVRG) an, das noch im November 2026 im Wiener Landtag beschlossen werden soll und am 1. Jänner 2027 in Kraft tritt. Bestehende Gastgeber haben eine Übergangsfrist bis Ablauf des 1. Quartals 2027, neue Gastgeber unterliegen ab 1. Jänner 2027 der Pflicht. Registrierungsnummer muss in Inseraten angegeben werden, Plattformen dürfen nur registrierte Wohnungen anbieten. Strafen bis 50.000 Euro pro Verstoß, bei Wiederholung Mindeststrafen von 2.000 Euro. Umwidmung in Beherbergungsstätten: mindestens 80 Prozent der Nutzflächen der Regelgeschoße müssen Wohnzwecken dienen, gilt für Verfahren seit Sommer 2026. 2025: 305 Anträge zu Beherbergungsstätten, 132 bewilligt; 2.484 Anzeigen seit Juli 2024, 558 Strafanträge bis Ende Juli 2026. Hinweis: die Seite trägt in den Metadaten das Datum 2024-11-21, der Text ist von September 2026 (Datum aus OTS übernommen).

name: EU opens Digital Services Act investigation into Booking.com over scams
text: The Next Web (Ana-Maria Stanciuc): the Commission opened its first formal DSA investigation into Booking.com, announced Wednesday 21 October 2026, on three areas: fake listings, protection of reservation and guest data shared with hosts (phishing), and labelling of paid-for higher-ranked listings. Booking.com reports over 45 million monthly EU users; fines up to 6% of annual global turnover; no fixed deadline; commitments possible. Booking.com says it is cooperating fully. Context: Meta DSA scam-ads probe since 2024, X fined EUR 120 million.

name: About the pay-per-booking (PPB) model
text: Vrbo Help Center page (primary source; the 2026-01-01 date is a page-date placeholder, the text reflects the post-29-Oct-2026 model). Under pay-per-booking Vrbo charges 12% on the rental amount plus host-charged fees such as cleaning, pet and boat fees. No commission on Vrbo traveler service fees, taxes, refundable deposits or insurance. With Vrbo's merchant-of-record service, the 12% is all-in with no separate processing fee; hosts with their own processor pay 12% plus that processor's fees. In some regions (parts of Europe, Australia, New Zealand) hosts on the Professional Plan may pay up to 15% including processing. VAT is added where it applies; in Australia, Japan and New Zealand 12% plus GST rules apply (Australia 0.5%, NZ 0.75% effective GST on commission).

name: Airbnb house rules policy (reasonable house rules and requests)
text: Platform rule effective 20 Nov 2026 for reservations booked on or after that date: hosts choose from seven standard house rules, generally may not ask guests to wash dishes, strip beds or take out garbage, may not fine guests, add rules after booking or collect guest IDs without a legal, building or insurer requirement. Amended 3 Nov 2026 (requests renamed additional rules). Compliance reviews 20 Nov 2026 to March 2027.

name: Bauordnung für Wien: Verschärfung Umwidmung in Beherbergungsstätten (§ 7g)
text: 80 Prozent Wohnnutzfläche, mindestens drei Zimmereinheiten, gesonderter Straßenzugang, Mindeststrafen 2.000 Euro bei Wiederholung.

name: Consumo requirement to two platforms: remove 8,318 seasonal-rental listings (22 Oct 2026)
text: Consumo asked two platforms to remove 8,318 tourist listings advertised as seasonal lets with bookings under 31 days (6,772 in Comunidad de Madrid, 6,523 in Madrid city); notified via DSA notice mechanisms; non-removal could lead to a sanctioning file.

name: Consumo requirement to two platforms: remove 8,352 tourist-rental listings without valid registration (12 Nov 2026)
text: Consumo told two unnamed large platforms to remove 8,352 listings: 7,199 on the first (6,263 no registration number, 936 false) and 1,153 on the second (964 none, 189 false). False numbers are extinct room-rental registrations used for whole units. Separate letter to Madrid on 4,443 listings blocked in Spain but visible abroad.

name: Consumo sanction on Airbnb: EUR 64 million, 65,000+ listings removed
text: Earlier Consumo sanction on Airbnb for non-compliant tourist listings (per Consumo, Oct 2026 release).

name: Digital Services Act
text: EU regulation setting rules for online platforms on illegal content, risks and ad transparency; stricter for very large online platforms (fines up to 6% of global annual turnover).

name: Real Decreto-ley 29/2026 (seasonal rentals minimum 31 days)
text: Approved by the Council of Ministers on 6 Oct 2026; amends the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos, seasonal rentals at least 31 days.

name: Vrbo flat 12% host commission
text: Flat 12% pay-per-booking commission replacing 5% (PMS) / 5%+3% processing (non-PMS) and annual subscriptions, for bookings from 29 Oct 2026; rollout staggered per account; subscribers move at term end; up to 15% in parts of Europe/Australia/NZ (Professional Plan). Whether processing is included is stated as all-in by Vrbo's help page and Hostaway/Hospitable; Futurestay saw a conflicting 3% processing line on an earlier version of the help page.

name: Vrbo host terms rate parity and 30-day direct booking clause
text: Host terms effective 29 Oct 2026: rates, discounts and fees given to Vrbo must be at least as favorable as on the host's own site and other channels; Vrbo may charge commission on direct bookings made within 30 days of a Vrbo inquiry. Limits channel-specific Vrbo markups above direct prices.

name: Wiener Kurzzeitvermietungsregistergesetz (WKVRG)
text: Wiener Landesgesetz: elektronisches Register für Kurzzeitvermietungen mit Registrierungsnummer, Pflichten für Plattformen, Strafen bis 50.000 Euro. Begleitend Änderung der Bauordnung für Wien.

Ab Freitag gelten Airbnbs neue Hausregeln
text: Für Buchungen ab dem 20. November dürfen Gastgeber Gästen in der Regel keine Putzarbeiten mehr auferlegen. Nach Protest hat Airbnb die Regel schon einmal gelockert.

name: Brüssel prüft Booking.com nach dem DSA
text: Die EU-Kommission hat am 21. Oktober ein förmliches Verfahren eröffnet: Betrugsinserate, Phishing mit Buchungsdaten und bezahlte Platzierungen ohne Werbekennzeichnung.

name: Wien: Kein Inserat ohne Registrierungsnummer, Frist bis Ende März
text: Laut ORF Wien hat der Landtag das Kurzzeitvermietungsregistergesetz beschlossen. Ab 1. Januar 2027 brauchen neue Inserate eine Nummer, bestehende ab April.

name: Bali-Registrierung greift

props.claim: Bis zum 30.06.2027 verkündet eine indonesische Behörde (national oder Provinz Bali) eine Frist oder Durchsetzungsmaßnahme für Registrierung, Lizenz oder Steuer bei Villa- und Kurzzeitvermietungen in Bali, die ausdrücklich Online-Plattformen oder Betreiber betrifft.

history.why: Der Druck auf nicht lizenzierte Villenvermietung in Bali wächst. Unklar bleibt, wann es zu einer konkreten Durchsetzung kommt. Startwert, wird mit Belegen angepasst.

name: KI-Gästeservice wird Standard

props.claim: Bis zum 31.03.2027 bieten mindestens drei der großen PMS-Anbieter (Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable, Lodgify, Smoobu) eine allgemein verfügbare KI-Funktion für Gästenachrichten in ihren Standardplänen an, offiziell angekündigt auf der Produktseite oder im Newsroom.

history.why: Mehrere Anbieter haben KI-Messaging bereits als Zusatz im Angebot. Offen ist nur, wie schnell es in die Standardpläne wandert.
Erste Lektüre: keiner der fünf bietet KI-Antworten nachweislich im Standardplan; Hospitable nur im Top-Plan Mogul, Lodgify Entwürfe, Smoobu nur Übersetzung; Hostaway/Guesty nur über Dritte belegt.

name: PMS-Konsolidierung

props.claim: Bis zum 30.06.2027 gibt mindestens ein großer PMS- oder Channel-Manager-Anbieter für Kurzzeitvermietung (Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable, Lodgify, Smoobu o.ä.) eine Übernahme eines anderen PMS-Anbieters oder eine Übernahme durch einen größeren Käufer öffentlich bekannt.

history.why: Der Markt ist fragmentiert, Funding ist knapper, Konsolidierung in Hospitality-Software ist ein wiederkehrendes Muster. Startwert, wird mit Belegen angepasst.
Guesty hat am 17. September 2026 den französischen PMS Smily (ex BookingSync) übernommen, zwei Monate vor Eröffnung der These. Solche Deals sind also kein Ausnahmefall; der Startwert war zu tief.
